MÉRIDA · YUCATÁN

Hot afternoons.
Music in the squares.

Our Mérida checklist. The old centre and the Paseo de Montejo once the heat drops, free music and dancing most nights, a birthday day off at Chichén Itzá with a cenote swim, and a Saturday at Uxmal.

No rushing required. Mornings are for work and the hottest hours are for staying in. Late afternoons and evenings take one outing at a time, in any order. The birthday Tuesday and the Saturdays are the only full days out.

BEFORE WE GO

Just a little planning

Heat. After San Cristóbal this is another climate: around 30°C by day in December and about 19°C at night. Walk early or after 5pm, and carry water.

Getting around. The centre is walkable and the streets are numbered. Uber and DiDi both work here. City buses (Va y Ven) take a rechargeable card, not cash.

Book ahead. Huniik needs a reservation. Decide between bus and tour for Chichén Itzá, and whether Uxmal is by bus or with a driver. Both ruins want cash: two tickets at two windows.

Chichén Itzá is on a Tuesday we took off, so one Saturday is still free. Celestún or El Cuyo could take it.

If you can afford to and would like to, consider donating to Red Nacional de Refugios to support women and children experiencing domestic violence.

I don’t receive any money or commission from these donations. Supporting local women matters to me, and this is one small way to give back to the places I visit. It takes all of us to stand against gender-based and domestic violence.
